summary: US-001: Platform scaffold — one command, all services up
description:
**As** a developer, **I want** a monorepo where `docker compose up` starts the five Go services, gateway, storefront and scanner shells with health checks, and `make check` runs the full local gate.

This is the prefactoring slice: it defines the repo layout, the gate (`make check` becomes `config.code.localGate`) and CI. It also supersedes the Python-scaffold docs (`docs/{configuration,development,docker,testing}.md`) with Go/TS equivalents.

**Priority:** P0
**Depends on:** —

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `docker compose up` from a clean clone brings up gateway + 5 service skeletons + storefront + scanner shell; `/healthz` green on all
- [ ] Storefront placeholder page served through the gateway in a browser
- [ ] `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS) passes, and fails correctly on seeded lint/test errors; documented in README; CI runs the same gate
- [ ] Services emit structured JSON logs with correlation/trace IDs propagated across service calls; a local tracing/metrics stack runs in Compose (concrete tooling chosen in the plan)
- [ ] Repo layout + service ownership documented in docs/architecture.md

Quality gates: `make check` green (defined in US-001, mirrors CI); contract tests for touched service boundaries; UI: browser-verified with screenshot in PR; money paths: NF525 journal chain verifies (from US-004).

*Planning note:* the US-001 plan must propose the database(s) and event bus as an ADR, approved at the plan gate.

binding.rule: We adopt Go for all backend services and TypeScript + React for the three frontends (storefront, back office, scanner). Money is represented as integer minor units + ISO currency code everywhere; floats are banned on money paths.

We build five Go services (catalog, inventory, commerce, payments, access) behind an API gateway, with an event bus for the domain event stream; every entity carries a tenant/organizer id from day one. Docker Compose only.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Execution plan — TKT-25 (US-001: Platform scaffold)

**Branch:** `TKT-25-platform-scaffold` · **Base:** origin/main (docs-only repo; everything below is new code)

#### Test seam (chosen first)
No code exists, so a new seam is unavoidable. Chosen seam: **the composed stack's HTTP surface through the gateway** — one integration smoke suite (`make smoke`, included in `make check`) that talks only to the gateway against `docker compose up`. Everything the ACs promise is observable there: per-service `/healthz`, the storefront page, and trace-ID propagation (asserted from the services' JSON logs). One seam, highest level, exercised exactly the way a user/CI would. Unit tests below it are minimal (middleware behavior only).

#### Proposed ADR-007 — Databases & event bus (approved with this plan, per ticket note)
- **Database: PostgreSQL 17** — one Compose container, **one database per service** (5 DBs, per-service credentials; no cross-DB queries). Rationale: the inventory hot path needs real transactional primitives (row locks/advisory locks for contention-safe claims, US-003); the ADR-003 append-only journal maps directly to Postgres append-only tables + triggers forbidding UPDATE/DELETE; one engine keeps the Compose estate and AI-tooling surface small. Database-per-service (not schema-per-service) keeps ADR-002 boundaries honest — a service literally cannot join another's tables. Rejected: SQLite (no concurrent-writer story for the hot path), one shared DB (boundary erosion), engine-per-service (operational tax with no payoff at this scale).
- **Event bus: NATS JetStream** — single small binary, first-class Compose citizen, persistent streams cover the ADR-003/TKT-24 domain-event stream, subject hierarchy fits per-tenant/per-domain routing. Rejected: Kafka/Redpanda (operational weight unjustified before TKT-24's analytics volume exists — revisit there), Postgres outbox-only (not a bus; outbox pattern still used *inside* services to publish reliably later — out of US-001 scope).
- US-001 only proves both run + are reachable (health checks, one demo publish/subscribe at boot); no domain schema yet.

#### Tooling decisions baked into this plan
- **Gateway: thin Go service** (stdlib `net/http` + `httputil.ReverseProxy`), not Traefik/Caddy — ADR-002 treats the gateway as first-class and later epics put logic there (waiting room TKT-20, aggregation ADR-004); starting it as our own Go service avoids a migration later. Routes: `/api/<service>/*` → service; `/` → storefront; `/healthz/all` → fan-out to all five services (this call is the trace-propagation demo).
- **Observability: OpenTelemetry + `grafana/otel-lgtm`** (one container: Grafana+Tempo+Loki+Prometheus). Go: `log/slog` JSON handler enriched with `trace_id`/`span_id`, `otelhttp` middleware on every service, W3C traceparent propagation. Satisfies the observability AC with a single extra container.
- **Go: 1.24+, one module per service + `shared/go` module, `go.work`; golangci-lint.** **TS: pnpm workspace, Vite + React shells for storefront & scanner, eslint + tsc; vitest.** Storefront shell is a deliberately disposable placeholder — TKT-39 decides the real shell (Astro vs SPA); nothing here may presuppose that outcome.
- **CI: GitHub Actions**, single workflow `on: {push: {branches: [main]}, pull_request}`, runs exactly `make check`.

#### Repo layout (documented in docs/architecture.md)
```
services/{catalog,inventory,commerce,payments,access}/   # Go, one module each: cmd/, internal/
gateway/                                                 # Go module
web/{storefront,scanner}/                                # TS/React shells (pnpm workspace)
shared/go/                                               # slog+otel middleware, healthz handler
deploy/compose.yaml                                      # everything incl. postgres, nats, otel-lgtm
scripts/gate-selftest.sh                                 # seeded-failure check
Makefile                                                 # check = lint+test+build+smoke
```

#### Steps (TDD order)
1. `shared/go`: healthz handler + slog/otel middleware, with unit tests (trace_id present in log records; traceparent propagated on outbound calls).
2. Five service skeletons + gateway consuming `shared/go`; each: `/healthz` (checks its DB conn; inventory also checks NATS), Dockerfile (multi-stage, distroless).
3. `deploy/compose.yaml`: 5 services + gateway + postgres (init script creating 5 DBs/roles) + nats (jetstream on) + otel-lgtm + storefront + scanner; healthchecks + depends_on conditions.
4. Web shells: storefront placeholder page + scanner placeholder (Vite React), served through the gateway.
5. Smoke suite (Go test, build-tagged `smoke`): gateway `/healthz/all` green for all 5; storefront HTML 200 via gateway; one trace ID observed in ≥2 services' logs for the fan-out call.
6. `Makefile` (`check` = lint+test+build+smoke) + `scripts/gate-selftest.sh` (applies seeded lint error + failing test patches, asserts `make check` fails, cleans up) + CI workflow running `make check` and the selftest.
7. Docs: rewrite `docs/{configuration,development,docker,testing}.md` for Go/TS; real architecture diagram + service-ownership table in `docs/architecture.md`; README quickstart; write `docs/adr/ADR-007-postgres-nats.md` (Accepted at this gate); update `.claude/sdlc.config.json` `code.localGate` → `make check`.

#### DoD
All 5 ticket ACs demonstrated: compose-up-from-clean-clone (verified in CI, which is a clean clone by construction), storefront page screenshot in PR (browser), `make check` green + selftest proving it fails on seeded errors, JSON logs with propagated trace IDs visible in Grafana/Loki + asserted by smoke test, docs updated. Contract tests: n/a this ticket (no domain API surface yet — healthz only); the contract-test harness lands with the first real contract (US-002).

#### Test plan
- Unit (Go): shared middleware — log record carries trace_id; outbound client injects traceparent; healthz handler contract.
- Integration (the seam): smoke suite against the composed stack, part of `make check` locally and in CI.
- Gate self-test: `scripts/gate-selftest.sh` — seeded golangci-lint violation, seeded failing Go test, seeded eslint violation; each must make `make check` exit non-zero.
- Browser: storefront + scanner placeholder pages through the gateway; Grafana shows a trace for `/healthz/all`. Screenshots in PR.

#### Risks / notes
- **Size**: readiness review flagged this story as oversized; the observability AC grew it again. Split-on-balloon valve: if the otel stack fights back, cut scope to logs-with-trace-ids + collector only, and move dashboards to a follow-up ticket rather than slipping.
- **CI wall-clock**: compose-in-CI is the slow step; images are stdlib-only Go + Vite, target < 10 min total.
- Storefront shell is throwaway by design (TKT-39); the scanner shell shares no framework commitment either.

#### Decisions you are approving at this gate (veto any individually)
1. ADR-007: PostgreSQL 17, database-per-service · NATS JetStream as the event bus.
2. Gateway built as our own thin Go service (not Traefik/Caddy).
3. Observability tooling: OpenTelemetry SDK + grafana/otel-lgtm single container.
4. `make check` becomes `config.code.localGate`; CI = GitHub Actions running the same target.

**Out of scope (explicitly):** `backoffice` frontend (ADR-002 lists it; US-001's AC does not — it lands with TKT-22), any domain API/schema, contract-test harness (first real contract is US-002), real PSP, auth.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan-final -->
### Final plan — TKT-25 (US-001: Platform scaffold) — post Codex critique

Codex (gpt-5.6) returned 20 findings: 9 blocking, 7 minor, 4 questions. **All 9 blocking accepted** and folded in below; triage of the rest at the end. This comment supersedes the `kind=plan` comment; unchanged parts (ADR-007 DB/bus proposal, Go gateway decision, repo layout, TDD step order, docs scope) carry over.

#### Revisions (by critique finding #)
1. **Compose file lives at the repo root** (`compose.yaml`) so the literal documented command `docker compose up` works from a clean clone. `deploy/` dropped.
2. **`make smoke` owns the stack lifecycle**: `docker compose -p ticketing-smoke up -d --build --wait` → run suite → `compose down -v` (teardown trapped). `make check` = lint → test → build → smoke, in that order; CI runs exactly `make check` on a runner with no pre-seeded caches — the smoke target *is* the literal clean-clone path (also answers #7).
3. **`/healthz` on every component**: five services + gateway (self-status, independent of downstreams) + storefront and scanner (served by nginx-alpine with a `/healthz` location). Gateway additionally exposes `/healthz/all` (fan-out).
4. **Log pipeline made real**: Go services use a slog→OTel bridge — every record goes to stdout (JSON, asserted by smoke) *and* via OTLP to the otel-lgtm collector (visible in Loki/Grafana). No Docker log scraping needed.
5. **Metrics made real**: `otelhttp` server metrics exported via OTLP; smoke asserts through the otel-lgtm Prometheus query API that `http.server.request.duration` (or equivalent) exists for ≥1 service after traffic.
6. **Distroless healthchecks**: each service binary gets a `healthcheck` subcommand (hits its own `/healthz` over localhost); compose healthchecks exec the binary — no shell/curl required.
8. **Gate self-test hardened**: runs in a disposable `git worktree` copy (never the developer's tree), trap-based cleanup, one seeded failure per gate stage verified independently: golangci-lint, failing `go test`, eslint, failing vitest (#9), `tsc` build error. Each must independently make `make check` exit non-zero.
11. **Deterministic bus proof**: nats bootstrap provisions a `PLATFORM` JetStream stream; the smoke suite publishes and durably consumes its own message (proves JetStream persistence), and **all five services** include NATS connectivity in `/healthz` (not just inventory, #12).
12. **DB boundary proof**: every service's `/healthz` verifies its own DB; smoke additionally asserts credential isolation (service A's role cannot connect to service B's database — expect failure).
16. **`/healthz/all` semantics defined**: 2s per-downstream timeout, concurrent fan-out, JSON `{service: up|down|timeout}`, 200 iff all up else 503. Gateway's compose healthcheck uses its *self* `/healthz` — no circularity. This endpoint remains the trace-propagation demo (same trace_id asserted in ≥2 services' logs).
19. **Storefront placeholder is plain static HTML** (nginx) — zero framework commitment ahead of the TKT-39 Astro-vs-SPA spike. The **scanner** shell is the Vite+React+vitest workspace (its stack is settled by ADR-001), so the TS toolchain is still established without biasing the spike.
15. **Gateway routes are an explicit registration table** (scaffold-only pass-through, noted in code + architecture doc), not a generic `/api/<service>/*` convention.

#### Triage of remaining findings
- **#13 (shared Postgres cluster) — accepted into ADR-007 text**: records the one-cluster/five-databases trade-off (no independent failure/upgrade/scaling boundaries) + separation triggers (inventory contention evidence from US-003/TKT-4 load tests, or divergent tuning needs).
- **#14 — accepted**: ADR-007 wording will cite Postgres's *fitness* for the ADR-003 journal but explicitly defer journal design (hash chain, signing, projections) to US-004.
- **#17 — accepted (wording)**: the gateway suite is the *primary* seam; infra assertions (credential isolation, JetStream, telemetry queries) are named auxiliary checks inside the same smoke suite, not hidden.
- **#18 — accepted (clarified)**: automated gate coverage = smoke assertions (storefront HTML via gateway, scanner 200, metrics/logs queries); manual PR evidence = browser screenshots (storefront, scanner, Grafana trace). Both listed in the PR.
- **#20 — accepted**: the split valve now only defers *dashboard curation* (custom Grafana boards → TKT-37); the tracing+metrics stack itself is acceptance scope and cannot be cut.
- **#10 (port collisions) — answered**: dev stack uses project name `ticketing` with documented fixed ports; `make smoke` uses `-p ticketing-smoke` with its own ephemeral published ports (env-overridable), owns its teardown, never touches the dev stack.
- **Rejected: none.**

#### Pre-mortem (lens applied, per quality-practices §1)
Lens: pre-mortem, run before the critique — it added the "decisions you are approving" list and the explicit backoffice out-of-scope note. The Codex pass then caught the operational gaps above (mostly lifecycle/ingestion realism) that the inside view missed — the two-pass design did its job.

#### Decisions you are approving at this gate (veto any individually)
1. **ADR-007**: PostgreSQL 17 — one Compose cluster, one database + role per service (trade-off + separation triggers recorded) · NATS JetStream as the event bus.
2. Gateway built as our own thin Go service (explicit route table; not Traefik/Caddy).
3. Observability: OTel SDK (traces+metrics+log bridge, OTLP) + `grafana/otel-lgtm`; storefront placeholder static-HTML-only pending TKT-39.
4. `make check` becomes `config.code.localGate`; CI = GitHub Actions running exactly `make check`.

**Out of scope:** backoffice frontend (TKT-22), domain APIs/schemas, contract-test harness (US-002), real PSP, auth, journal design (US-004).

**Estimated size warning stands** (readiness review): this is the accepted-oversized scaffold slice; the only remaining valve is deferring dashboard curation to TKT-37.

### Plan amendment (owner steering, 2026-07-12) — supersedes prior plan-final on these points only

1. **ADR-007: PostgreSQL 18.4** (was 17). Cluster/database-per-service design unchanged.
2. **New standing policy (owner directive): latest stable versions by default, platform-wide.** Greenfield project — every language, runtime and dependency (Go, Node, TypeScript, Vite, Postgres, Redis, NATS, tooling) targets its latest stable release; versions are looked up at implementation time, not assumed. Deviations require a stated compatibility reason. Applies to this ticket's Dockerfiles, go.mod, package.json, CI, and to ADR-007's wording; will be recorded in docs/conventions during this ticket's docs step.

Everything else in the prior plan-final stands. Ticket remains at Gate 2 awaiting plan approval.
